social_formats.description: Outdoor processional group march followed by a circular ring dance around a pole

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Arms held high carrying poles, banners, or props; joining hands in a circle during ring dance.
movement_profile.footwork: Rhythmic stepping, step-hops, and simple circular walking patterns.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Linear processional outdoor street path ending in a circular ring dance around a central pole.
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Natural torso movement aligned with processional locomotion.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Ground-level stepping with occasional celebratory hops or skips.
movement_profile.partnering: Communal group circle; no formal individual partnering required during the core wren pole dance.
movement_profile.posture: Upright, energetic processional stance, transitioning to hand-in-hand open ring posture.

signature_moves.description: Dancers join hands to circle a central decorated pole carrying the wren.
signature_moves.name: Wren Pole Circling

movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid modern choreography styling; keep movements grounded in traditional communal processional folk forms.

music_profile.musical_form: Strophic song verses alternating with lively dance reel or jig sections
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Driving pulse punctuated by bodhrán accents and fife melody lines
music_profile.sound_description: Bright acoustic folk sound dominated by rhythmic frame-drum beat, lively melodeon chords, high-pitched fife or whistle tunes, and spirited group singing.
music_profile.vocal_style: Group chorus chanting, begging song call-and-response, or traditional sean-nós ornamentation

basic_steps: Processional step-hop or lively walking step in procession behind the wren pole
Ring formation joining hands around the central wren bush
Clockwise and counter-clockwise circular stepping in time to drum rhythms
teaching.formation: Processional parade line leading into a central open circle (ringelreihen)
teaching.level_notes: Accessible community folk steps emphasizing communal participation and rhythmic group walking/circling.
teaching.rhythm: Lively duple or compound meter typical of Irish/Manx folk dance tunes (reels/jigs)
